2027-05-07.title: The Finding of the Cross of our Lord · First Friday · Friday after Suloko
readings: May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ
The treasure hidden in a field; the pearl of great value
2027-05-07.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), after Suloko (the Ascension): the ten days of waiting and prayer for the Holy Spirit before Pentecost. The Panchangam notes that weddings are not celebrated in these days. The Panchangam keeps today the Finding of the Cross of our Lord. It is also the First Friday of May.
2027-05-07.verse: May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
theo: Yesterday the Church watched the Lord go up into heaven. Today, on the first day of the ten days of waiting, the Panchangam turns our eyes back to the wood on which he died: it keeps the Finding of the Cross of our Lord. This is not a step backwards. The one who ascended is the Crucified; he carries the marks of the nails into the glory of the Father, and the Cross is the road by which he went up. Our Malankara tradition calls the Cross the Sleeba, and we never pray without it: we sign ourselves at the beginning and the end of every prayer, the priest blesses with the hand cross, and the bare cross on our altars, without a figure, proclaims that the Crucified is risen. What can be said with confidence about the finding is this. In the reign of the emperor Constantine, the place of Golgotha and the tomb had been uncovered in Jerusalem and a great church built over them. St Cyril of Jerusalem, preaching there around 350, could already say that the wood of the Cross had been distributed in fragments over the whole world (Catechetical Lectures 4.10; 13.4, in substance). By the end of that century St Ambrose of Milan told how St Helena, Constantine's mother, had searched Golgotha and found the Cross (On the Death of Theodosius 43–46, in substance). The details belong to tradition; the heart of the feast is certain. The Cross is not lost. It was found, and it is found again whenever a Christian chooses it.

St Paul ends his letter to the Galatians in his own handwriting: “See what large letters I make when I am writing in my own hand!” He has argued at length with those who wanted the Gentile converts to be circumcised, and now he gathers everything into one sentence: “May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.” To boast is to rest your worth on something. People boast of family, money, education, the size of their house or their church. Paul rests his whole worth on the Cross, where the Son of God “loved me and gave himself for me” (Galatians 2:20). Then he adds: “For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything; but a new creation is everything!” The Cross makes new creatures. And he closes with a line that only a man who had been beaten and stoned could write: “I carry the marks of Jesus branded on my body.” St John Chrysostom, commenting here, said that what seems a reproach to the world is for Paul the cause of countless blessings, and so he glories in it (Commentary on Galatians 6, in substance). The Cross is the place where the world's values are turned upside down: weakness becomes strength, shame becomes glory, death becomes life.

The Gospel gives the feast its picture. “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which someone found and hid; then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.” The finder does not sell everything grudgingly; he does it “in his joy.” So it is with the Cross. To the world it looks like loss; to the one who has found it, it is the treasure that makes everything else worth selling. The merchant who finds “one pearl of great value” does the same. On this First Friday many of our parishes keep the devotion to the Sacred Heart: the Heart of Jesus opened on the Cross, from which “at once blood and water came out” (John 19:34), the Church's sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Qurbono. The Catechism says that the Heart of Jesus, pierced by our sins and for our salvation, is the sign and symbol of the love with which he loves us (CCC 478). Make the sign of the Cross today slowly and with attention. Go to confession if you can, and take part in the Holy Qurbono. And in these ten days, as we wait for the Spirit, ask for the grace to boast of nothing but the Cross, and to find in it the hidden treasure of your life.
conn: Numbers 21:8–9 and John 3:14–15: the bronze serpent on the pole, which healed those who looked at it, foreshadowed the Son of Man lifted up on the Cross.
Matthew 13:44 and Philippians 3:8: Paul counted everything as loss for the surpassing value of knowing Christ crucified and risen.
Zechariah 12:10 and John 19:34–37: they shall look on the one whom they have pierced; from his opened side came blood and water.
fathers: Let us not be ashamed of the Cross of Christ; even if others hide it, seal it openly on your forehead, so that the demons may see the royal sign and flee trembling far away (Catechetical Lectures 13.36, in substance).

What seems a reproach to the world is to Paul the cause of countless blessings; therefore he glories in the Cross, by which he died to the world and the world to him (Commentary on Galatians 6, in substance).
magis: The Cross is the unique sacrifice of Christ, the one mediator between God and men; he calls his disciples to take up their cross and follow him, for Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example.
Jesus knew and loved us each and all during his life, his agony and his Passion; the Sacred Heart of Jesus, pierced by our sins and for our salvation, is the sign and symbol of that love.
The Christian begins his day, his prayers and his activities with the sign of the Cross, dedicating the day to the glory of God.
outline: Ask: what do I boast of, what do I rest my worth on?
Point 1 · Boasting only in the Cross
Paul's own handwriting, the new creation, and the marks of Jesus.
Point 2 · A treasure hidden in a field
The Cross found in Jerusalem and found again in every heart that chooses it.
First Friday: blood and water from the opened side.
“May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.”
live: Make the sign of the Cross slowly and attentively each time you begin and end a prayer today.
Go to confession if you can, take part in the Holy Qurbono, or spend some minutes before the Blessed Sacrament for the Heart of Jesus.
2027-05-07.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen and ascended, you carried the marks of your Cross into the glory of the Father. On this day of the Finding of your Cross we thank you for the holy wood on which you redeemed the world. Let us boast of nothing but your Cross; crucify the world to us and us to the world, and make us a new creation. Show us the hidden treasure and give us the joy to sell all for it. From your pierced Heart pour out on us the blood and water of your mercy, and as we wait for the Holy Spirit, keep us under the sign of the Cross. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The sacrifice of the Cross is made present on our altar in the Holy Qurbono; the bare cross above it tells us that the Crucified is risen and feeds us with his Body and Blood.

quick: The Panchangam keeps today the Finding of the Cross; by about 350 St Cyril of Jerusalem spoke of fragments of the wood spread through the world, and tradition links the finding with St Helena.
Paul boasts of nothing but the Cross, by which the world is crucified to him; what matters is a new creation.
The kingdom is a treasure hidden in a field; on this First Friday we honour the pierced Heart of Jesus.
2027-05-07.action: Make the sign of the Cross slowly and attentively each time you pray today.
2027-05-07.question: What do I really boast of, and does it lead me to the Cross or away from it?
term: The Syriac word for the Cross. In our Church the bare Sleeba, without a figure, stands on the altar and is used for blessing, proclaiming that the Crucified One is risen.
kidsaint: St Helena was the mother of the emperor Constantine. When she was old, she travelled to Jerusalem to visit the places where Jesus had lived, died and risen. An old story tells that she searched on the hill of Calvary and found the Cross of Jesus. Lesson: every time you make the sign of the Cross, you are holding up the greatest treasure in the world, the sign of Jesus' love.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who found a treasure hidden in a field. He was so happy that he sold everything he had to buy that field! Today our Church remembers the finding of the Cross of Jesus. The Cross is our treasure, because on it Jesus showed how much he loves us. It is also First Friday, when we remember the Heart of Jesus, full of love for us.
family.intention: We pray for people who are carrying a heavy cross of sickness, sadness or poverty.
family.ask: Ask: “What is our family's greatest treasure? How can we show that Jesus is the most important?”

illus: A woman in Thiruvalla wore a small wooden cross on a thread for forty years, long after her friends had moved to gold chains. When her grandson asked why she did not wear something more beautiful, she told him that her mother had given it to her the day she left home to work as a nurse in the Gulf. On nights in a strange land, when she was afraid or lonely, she held it in her hand. “Gold I could lose,” she said. “This kept me.” The day she died, the family placed the same little cross in her hands.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Let us boast of nothing but your Cross. Amen.
share: May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ (Galatians 6:14). What do I boast of instead?
In his joy he goes and sells all that he has (Matthew 13:44). What would I give up for the treasure of Christ?
I carry the marks of Jesus branded on my body (Galatians 6:17). What marks of suffering for Christ do I carry, and how can I offer them?
pm.resp: We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.
interc: For all who carry heavy crosses of illness, loss or poverty, that they may find in the Cross of Christ their strength.
For Christians in the Holy Land and in Jerusalem, where the Cross was raised and found.
For those who are ashamed of their faith, that they may sign themselves openly with the Cross.
On this First Friday, for sinners, that the pierced Heart of Jesus may draw them to repentance.
For our parish in these days of waiting, that we may receive the Holy Spirit with open hearts.
pm.close: Father, you willed that your Son should save the world by the Cross. As we honour the finding of the holy Cross, grant that we may share in its mystery here on earth and enjoy its fruit, the risen life, in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Yesterday we celebrated Suloko, the Ascension. Today the Panchangam keeps the Finding of the Cross of our Lord. The one who has gone up to the Father is the Crucified; the Cross was the road of his glory. Very early, by the time of St Cyril of Jerusalem around 350, pieces of the wood of the Cross were honoured throughout the world, and tradition tells that St Helena found it on Golgotha.

St Paul writes in large letters with his own hand: may I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world (Galatians 6:14). What matters is not outward marks but a new creation. Paul carried the marks of Jesus on his body; he was not ashamed of them.

In the Gospel Jesus says that the kingdom is like a treasure hidden in a field. A man finds it and in his joy sells everything to buy the field (Matthew 13:44). The Cross is that treasure. The world sees loss; the believer sees the love of God, and gladly gives up everything for it.

Today is also First Friday. We honour the Heart of Jesus, opened on the Cross, from which blood and water flowed. Let us make the sign of the Cross with love, go to confession, receive the Holy Qurbono, and in these days of waiting ask the Spirit to make us boast only of the Cross. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you like stories about hidden treasure? Jesus told one: a man found treasure buried in a field and was so happy that he sold everything to buy that field. Today we remember the day the Cross of Jesus was found. The Cross is our treasure, because it shows how much Jesus loves us. Every time you make the sign of the Cross, do it slowly and say in your heart: “Jesus, thank you for loving me!”

On the Finding of the Cross and First Friday, the day after Suloko: boasting only in the Cross, the treasure hidden in a field, and the pierced Heart of Jesus.

For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.

concl: The ascended Lord is the Crucified; the Cross is the road of his glory and of ours.
Whoever finds the Cross finds the treasure for which everything else may be gladly sold.
2027-05-07.resolve: Sign yourself with the Cross attentively, boast of nothing but Christ crucified, and bring your heart to his pierced Heart in these days of waiting.
